en: The Sūtra on the Merit Arising from Upholding the Names of the Seven Buddhas, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha, the Bhagavān, was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove.

In the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, he was accompanied by immeasurable and incalculable numbers of śrāvakas and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as all the great assemblies of devas, humans, asuras, and others, surrounding him on all sides.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra:

"Out of compassion for all sentient beings, I shall now briefly explain the merit produced by upholding the names of the seven Buddhas, so that those who uphold them shall obtain supreme benefit, peace, and happiness."
"You should listen attentively and reflect well!
I shall analyze and explain it for you.
Śāriputra said:
“Indeed, World-Honored One, we wish and desire to hear it.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“In this eastern direction, there is a buddha-field named Adorned with the Array of Stainless Multitudes of Virtues. In that land there is a Buddha named Sūryamaṇḍalavairocanaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavat. He currently resides there, out of compassion for the world, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly, revealing that which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end—its words and meanings are exquisite, pure, complete, and a holy life that is entirely white and immaculate.”

If there are those who hear the name of that Buddha, they shall transcend the intense suffering of wandering through the long night of birth and death for hundreds of thousands of *koṭis* of great eons; wherever they are born, they will always remember their past lives.

Those who are able to receive and uphold the name of that Buddha will not lose the merit previously obtained, and furthermore, for hundreds of thousands of *koṭis* of great eons, in whatever place they are born, their minds will be free from delusion, and they will experience various sublime joys among gods and humans.

Those who are able to establish images of that Buddha, making offerings, paying respect, honoring, and praising them, will not lose the merit previously obtained, and furthermore, for immeasurable *koṭis* of great eons, wherever they are born, they will always encounter Buddhas and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, there is another buddha-field named Adorned with the Multitude of Virtues of Sublime Awakening. In that land, there is a Buddha named Śrī-vihārin-guṇa-suvicitra Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān. He currently dwells there, out of compassion for the world, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the sake of gods and humans; he reveals the Dharma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with skillful phrasing and meaning, pure, complete, and a holy life that is utterly pristine."
If there are those who hear the name of that Buddha, they shall immediately transcend all eight difficult conditions and, wherever they are born, always remember their past lives.

Those who are able to receive and uphold the name of that Buddha will not lose the merits previously obtained; furthermore, for immeasurable *koṭis* of great eons, wherever they are born, their minds will always be sharp and wise, they will constantly dwell in the happy realms, and experience various sublime joys.

Those who are able to establish images of that Buddha, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, and praising them, will not lose the merits previously obtained; furthermore, for immeasurable *koṭis* of great eons, wherever they are born, they will always encounter Buddhas, practice all the *pāramitās*, and become great guides who deliver immeasurable multitudes.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, there is another buddha-field named Sattvapati. In that land there is a Buddha named Ekaratnacchattra-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān. He currently resides there, out of compassion for the world, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma to the great assembly, revealing that which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end; its phrasing and meaning are exquisite, it is pure, complete, and a holy life that is entirely stainless."

If there are those who hear the name of that Buddha, they shall immediately be far removed from all sorrow and suffering; their rank, office, wealth, and treasures shall never decline or be lost, except for the fixed causes of evil karma from past lives.

Those who are able to receive and uphold the name of that Buddha shall not lose the merits previously obtained; wherever they are born, they will possess great majesty and virtue, with supernormal powers at their command, bodies radiating light, and forms so upright and dignified that all delight in beholding them.

Those who are able to establish images of that Buddha, making offerings, paying homage, respecting, and praising them, shall likewise not lose the merits previously obtained; furthermore, throughout immeasurable *koṭi* of great eons, they shall never be born in worlds where no Buddha dwells, but shall cultivate the bodhisattva practices, adorned by great vows, and attain unsurpassed enlightenment to benefit all beings.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, there is another buddha-field named Sovereign Power (*Vaśitābala*). In that land there is a Buddha named Sugatavyavasthita-vyākaraṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavat. He currently resides there, out of compassion for the world, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma to the great assembly, revealing that which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end; its phrasing and meaning are exquisite, it is pure, complete, and constitutes the holy life of total purity."
If there are those who hear the name of that Buddha, their minds will immediately become tranquil and free from all clamor and distraction.

Those who are able to receive and uphold the name of that Buddha shall not lose the merit previously obtained; furthermore, for immeasurable *koṭi* great eons, in whatever place they are born and throughout the four modes of deportment—whether speaking or remaining silent—their minds will always abide in meditative concentration.

Those who are able to establish images of that Buddha, making offerings, paying respect, honoring, and praising them, shall not lose the merit previously obtained; furthermore, for immeasurable *koṭi* great eons, wherever they are born they will always encounter Buddhas, swiftly reach the ultimate realization of all gateways of samādhi, and become Honored Among Two-Legged Beings to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, there is another buddha-field named Most Excellent Jewel. In that land there is a Buddha named Ratnakusumaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān. He currently resides there, out of compassion for the world, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma to the great assembly, revealing that which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end; its words and meaning are exquisite, it is pure, complete, and a holy life that is entirely stainless."

If there are those who hear the name of that Buddha, they shall immediately attain the complete perfection of superior mindfulness, wisdom, and conduct; dwelling among the fourfold assembly, they shall preach the Dharma without fear, their words majestic and solemn, such that all who hear them receive them with reverence.

Those who are able to uphold the name of that Buddha shall not lose the merits previously obtained; furthermore, throughout immeasurable *koṭi* of great eons, wherever they are born, they shall possess mindfulness, wisdom, and conduct, achieve sharp and penetrating intelligence, and attain supreme retention of what is heard.

Whoever is able to establish an image of that Buddha, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising it, shall not lose the merit previously obtained; furthermore, for immeasurable *koṭi* of great eons, wherever they are born, they will always encounter a Tathāgata, possess unimpeded eloquence to widely proclaim the sublime Dharma, gradually cultivate the provisions of merit and wisdom, and become a Honored One among gods and humans who delivers immeasurable multitudes.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of here, there is a buddha-field named Śāntamaṇi. In that land there is a Buddha named Anantapadavikrāmin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Leader of Men, Tamer of Beings, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān. He currently resides there, out of compassion for the world, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma to the great assembly, revealing that which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end; its phrasing and meaning are exquisite, it is pure, complete, and a pristine holy life."
If there are those who hear the name of that Buddha, their minds will be serene and free from disturbance;

those who can receive and uphold his name shall not lose the merit previously obtained, and they will further be able to swiftly realize the supreme samādhi of Moonlight. Having realized this samādhi, they will immediately thereafter be able to realize as many gateways to samādhi as there are grains of sand in the Ganges.

Those who can construct images of that Buddha, making offerings, paying homage, respecting, and praising them, shall not lose the merit previously obtained; furthermore, regarding the Dharma-gates preached by all Buddhas, they will be able to fully receive and uphold them, penetrating their profound meanings and understanding them with unimpeded clarity like the light of the sun. Wherever they are born, they will always encounter Buddhas, and by means of this, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of here, there is another buddha-field named Most Excellent Fragrance (*Gandhottama*). In that land, there is a Buddha named King of Sublime Fragrance (*Gandharāja*) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān. He currently resides there, out of compassion for the world, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma to the great assembly, revealing that which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end; its words and meanings are exquisite, it is pure, complete, and the pristine holy life."

If there are those who hear the name of that Buddha, their bodies and minds will become harmonious and supple, they will be freed from all heaviness and rigidity, their evil karma will be extinguished, and their afflictions will become light and subtle.

Those who are able to receive and uphold the name of that Buddha shall not lose the merits previously obtained; furthermore, in future lives wherever they are born, they will be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man and will be gazed upon with reverence by all sentient beings.

Those who are able to establish images of that Buddha, making offerings, paying respect, honoring, and praising them, shall not lose the merits previously obtained; furthermore, in future lives wherever they are born, they will always leave the household life and attain pure precepts, travel through various Buddha-lands to hear and uphold the Dharma, and fully cultivate all meritorious virtues, thereby swiftly realizing *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"If any sentient beings hear the names of these seven Buddhas, uphold them, and make offerings to them, they will certainly obtain the merits previously described."

Why is this so? Because the names and physical forms of these seven Buddhas were all accomplished through their original vows and great compassion; thus, when sentient beings hear, uphold, and make offerings to them, they shall all obtain such benefits and peace and happiness.

When the Bhagavān had finished speaking this sutra, Śāriputra and the other great śrāvakas, as well as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, together with the entire assembly of devas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra on the Merit Arising from Upholding the Names of the Seven Buddhas.
